name: Langtang & Manaslu
tagline: Tamang, Hyolmo and Nubri country north of Kathmandu
meta_description: Langtang, Gosaikunda, Helambu, Nuwakot and Manaslu: treks, Tamang homestays and Tibetan-Buddhist valleys north of Kathmandu. Seasons, permits, 2026 flood update.
summary: Langtang and Manaslu are the mountains directly north of Kathmandu: Langtang Valley, Gosaikunda and Helambu in Bagmati Province, and the Manaslu Circuit and Tsum Valley in Gandaki. They offer treks of 2 to 24 days, Tamang and Hyolmo villages, Tibetan-Buddhist valleys and Nuwakot's palace. Parts of Rasuwa were devastated by the August 2026 flood.
intro: Draw a line north from Kathmandu and within 60 to 120 km you reach some of the most varied mountain country in Nepal. To the north-east lie the Shivapuri ridge, Chisapani and the Hyolmo villages of Helambu. Due north, Langtang National Park holds the Langtang Valley, the sacred lake of Gosaikunda and the Tamang villages of Rasuwa. Further west, beyond Ganesh Himal, the Budhi Gandaki leads to Manaslu, the world's eighth-highest mountain, and the Tibetan-Buddhist valleys of Nubri and Tsum.

This is a region without big airports or resort towns. You arrive by road and on foot. That keeps it close to the villages and people who live here: the Tamang, the largest community in the hills around Kathmandu; the Hyolmo of Helambu; the Langtangpa; and the Nubri and Tsumba of the Manaslu valleys. Their gompas, mani walls, homestays, Tamang Selo songs and yak-cheese kitchens are as much the point of a trip here as the peaks.

History runs through it too. Nuwakot's seven-storey palace is where Prithvi Narayan Shah planned the unification of Nepal in the 1740s. The Bhote Koshi valley was for centuries the trade road to Kerung in Tibet. Langtang village was destroyed by an avalanche in the 2015 earthquake and rebuilt by its own people, and Tsum's villages have kept a vow against killing animals for more than a century.

On 26 August 2026 a glacier collapse near Langtang Lirung sent a flood down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli, devastating Syabrubesi, Timure, Rasuwagadhi and parts of Nuwakot, with more than 1,400 people reported dead. Langtang trekking was suspended. Helambu, Chisapani and the Manaslu valleys lie on other rivers. We write this guide with respect for those lost; check current status before you travel.

story.title: Trade roads, kings, quakes and a flood
paras: For centuries the valleys north of Kathmandu were corridors to Tibet. The Bhote Koshi route through what is now Syabrubesi and Rasuwagadhi linked the Kathmandu Valley with Kerung, today's Gyirong, carrying salt and wool south and grain and goods north. Peoples on both sides of the border shared language and religion: the Hyolmo and Langtangpa speak Tibetic languages close to the speech of Kyirong, and Buddhist teachers moved freely between valleys regarded as beyul, hidden lands blessed by Guru Padmasambhava.

Whoever held the routes held power. In 1744 Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha seized the hill fort of Nuwakot from the Malla king of Kathmandu, built his seven-storey palace there and used it as the base for the conquest of the valley in 1768 and 1769. In 1792 Qing Chinese armies came down the Bhote Koshi as far as the hills above Nuwakot. In 1855 Nepal built the Rasuwagadhi fort on the border during its war with Tibet.

In the 20th century the region opened to the world on foot. Swiss development workers introduced cheese-making to Langtang in the 1950s; Japanese climbers made the first ascent of Manaslu in 1956; Langtang became Nepal's first Himalayan national park in 1976; the Manaslu Conservation Area followed in 1998; and Tsum opened to trekkers in 2008. Tamang and Hyolmo villages built lodges and homestays, and Langtang became one of Nepal's most popular treks.

Then came disaster, twice. On 25 April 2015 the Gorkha earthquake triggered an avalanche that buried Langtang village and killed hundreds. On 26 August 2026 a glacier collapse near Langtang Lirung sent a flood over 100 km down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli, destroying the border crossing, much of Syabrubesi and hydropower plants, with heavy loss of life. The people of Rasuwa and Nuwakot rebuilt once, and are rebuilding again.

legend: In Hindu tradition, Gosaikunda was created when Shiva, his throat burning from the poison he swallowed at the churning of the ocean, struck the mountain with his trident to bring out cold water. In Buddhist tradition, Langtang, Yolmo and Tsum are beyul, hidden valleys that Guru Padmasambhava blessed as refuges for hard times, and the yogi Milarepa is said to have meditated in caves in Tsum.
people: The Tamang are the largest community in Rasuwa and Nuwakot's hills, Buddhist with shamanic traditions, known for Tamang Selo music. The Hyolmo live in Helambu, the Langtangpa in the Langtang Valley, and the Nubri and Tsumba in the Manaslu valleys, all Tibetan-Buddhist with Tibetic languages. Newar, Brahmin and Chhetri families farm the lower valleys around Nuwakot.

untold.fact: Langtang National Park, gazetted in 1976, was Nepal's first Himalayan national park and its fourth protected area. In the north and east it adjoins the Qomolangma National Nature Preserve in Tibet.
Prithvi Narayan Shah's Gorkha army attacked Nuwakot on 26 September 1744, a date chosen by his astrologer, and took it within days. The fort became the base for the conquest of the Kathmandu Valley.
The Gosaikunda lake complex, about 1,030 hectares, was designated a Ramsar wetland of international importance on 29 September 2007.
Upper Tsum Valley declared itself a zone of non-violence toward animals in about 1920 under the Shyagya vow, and Lower Tsum's 22 settlements joined in 2012.
untold.source: The Himalayan Times: Sacred Tsum Valley gears up for centennial celebrations

untold.fact: The glacier collapse that caused the 26 August 2026 flood was so large that it registered as a seismic event of about magnitude 5.2, first mistaken for an earthquake. No rain had fallen that morning at the Rasuwa headquarters.

taste.name: Yak cheese, tsampa and Tamang dhindo
taste.text: Langtang's yak cheese, made at Kyanjin with methods brought by the Swiss in the 1950s, tsampa and butter tea in Langtang, Nubri and Tsum lodges, and millet dhindo with greens in Tamang homestays at Gatlang and Briddim. Helambu adds sweet apples in autumn; Nuwakot, river fish fried by the Trishuli.

highlights.title: Langtang Valley trek
highlights.text: Seven to eight days from Kathmandu to Kyanjin Gompa at 3,870 m and back, through forest, yak pastures and the rebuilt Langtang village, with Kyanjin Ri for views of Langtang Lirung. Road access to Syabrubesi was cut by the 2026 flood; check current status.

highlights.title: Gosaikunda
highlights.text: The sacred lake at 4,380 m where Shiva struck his trident, reached in two to three days from Dhunche. At Janai Purnima in August thousands of pilgrims and shamans gather to bathe at dawn.

highlights.title: Manaslu Circuit
highlights.text: Fourteen to sixteen days around the world's eighth-highest mountain, up the Budhi Gandaki through Nubri villages to Samagaon and over Larkya La at 5,106 m to Bhimthang. Restricted permits and a licensed guide are required.

highlights.title: Tsum Valley
highlights.text: A Tibetan-Buddhist valley opened to trekkers only in 2008, with Mu Gompa, Rachen nunnery, Milarepa's cave and a century-old vow against killing animals. Add it to the Manaslu Circuit or trek it on its own.

highlights.title: Tamang villages and Helambu
highlights.text: Homestays in Gatlang and Briddim on the Tamang Heritage Trail, and the Hyolmo villages, gompas and apple orchards of Helambu, reachable on foot from Kathmandu via Chisapani.

highlights.title: Nuwakot
highlights.text: Prithvi Narayan Shah's seven-storey palace on a ridge above the Trishuli, with the Bhairavi temple and the spring Sindure Jatra. One or two nights at a restored farmhouse make an easy history trip from Kathmandu.

getting_there: Everything here starts in Kathmandu, and almost everything by road. For Langtang, Gosaikunda and the Tamang Heritage Trail, the Pasang Lhamu Highway runs north over Kakani to Trishuli, Dhunche (about 117 km) and Syabrubesi (about 120 km), normally 6 to 9 hours. That corridor was devastated by the flood of 26 August 2026, with roads and bridges destroyed; detours via Dhunche were being assessed in September. For Helambu and Chisapani, drive 45 minutes to Sundarijal and walk, or take jeeps to Melamchi and upper villages. For Manaslu and Tsum, drive 8 to 9 hours via the Prithvi Highway and Arughat to Machha Khola or Soti Khola. Nuwakot is about 75 km, 3 to 3.5 hours. Check current status before you travel.
permits: Foreign visitors need the Langtang National Park entry permit for Langtang, Gosaikunda and upper Helambu, and the Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park fee for Chisapani. Manaslu requires a restricted area permit, issued through a registered agency for at least two trekkers with a guide, plus the Manaslu Conservation Area permit, and ACAP if exiting to Dharapani. Tsum has its own restricted permit. Since April 2023 foreign trekkers in national parks and conservation areas must trek with a licensed guide. Fees and rules change; check current status before you travel.

months.weather: Kathmandu 2–19 °C; Kyanjin to −15 °C at night, dry and clear
months.summary: Cold, clear and quiet. Lower treks such as Chisapani, Helambu and the Tamang Heritage Trail are good, with crisp mountain views and empty trails. Langtang is possible but lodges thin out above Langtang village, and Gosaikunda and Larkya La are often snowbound. Nuwakot is sunny and mild by day. Sonam Lhosar may fall at the end of the month, filling Tamang villages with music.
months.tip: Pack a sleeping bag rated to minus 15 °C for anything above 3,000 m.

months.summary: Still cold up high, but days lengthen and snow begins to settle. Sonam Lhosar often falls in February, a good time for a homestay in Gatlang or Briddim if road access allows. Helambu and Chisapani give clear views with few trekkers. Gosaikunda and Larkya La remain risky with snow. Nuwakot is pleasant for history and ridge walks.
months.tip: Check whether lodges are open before planning any trek above 3,500 m.

months.summary: Spring trekking begins. Rhododendrons start to bloom in the forests of Langtang and Helambu, and lodges reopen. Mornings are clear, with haze building by afternoon. The Manaslu Circuit opens up, though Larkya La can still carry snow. A strong month for Langtang Valley, Helambu and the Tamang Heritage Trail, access permitting.
months.tip: Start walking early to catch clear mountain views before midday haze.

months.weather: Kathmandu 11–28 °C; warm days, cold nights above 3,500 m
months.summary: Peak spring. Rhododendron forests are in full flower from 2,500 to 3,500 m, Langtang and Manaslu trails are busy and lodges are fully open. Nuwakot celebrates Sindure Jatra, with processions and red sindur powder. Haze is common at lower levels. Gosaikunda becomes reachable as snow melts, and Larkya La is usually crossable.
months.tip: Book Manaslu and Langtang lodges ahead for April.

months.weather: Kathmandu 16–29 °C; pre-monsoon showers by late month
months.summary: Warm and green. Good for high routes: Gosaikunda, Kyanjin Ri, Tsum Valley and Larkya La, before the monsoon. Afternoon cloud and showers increase toward the end of the month. Nuwakot's Sindure Jatra closes in early May. The valley floors around Nuwakot become hot, above 30 °C.
months.tip: Finish high passes by late May to avoid monsoon cloud and rain.

months.summary: Monsoon arrives. Roads to Syabrubesi, Dhunche and Arughat are prone to landslides, leeches fill the lower forests and mountain views disappear. High pastures turn green and herders move up with yaks, but we do not recommend trekking. Nuwakot can be visited on short trips between storms.
months.tip: If you must travel, keep plans flexible and carry rain gear and leech socks.

months.weather: Kathmandu 20–28 °C; heaviest rain of the year
months.summary: The wettest month. Roads in Rasuwa and Gorkha are frequently blocked, rivers run high and trails are slippery. In 2025 a glacial lake flood hit Rasuwagadhi in early July. Trekking is not advised. Flowering meadows above 3,500 m are beautiful but usually hidden in cloud.
months.tip: Avoid river-valley roads during heavy rain warnings.

months.summary: Still monsoon, but August brings Janai Purnima, when thousands of pilgrims climb to Gosaikunda for the full moon. It is a hard trip in rain and leeches, rewarding for those who go prepared. In August 2026 the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli flood struck Rasuwa and Nuwakot; check current status before planning any trip in the corridor.
months.tip: For Janai Purnima, leave Dhunche three days before the full moon.

months.weather: Kathmandu 19–27 °C; rain easing late in the month
months.summary: The monsoon fades through September. Late in the month the Manaslu Circuit and Tsum Valley begin their autumn season, with green terraces and fewer trekkers. Roads may still be damaged by landslides. In 2026, Rasuwa was in a declared disaster period after the August flood; check current status before you travel.
months.tip: Plan spare days for landslide delays on mountain roads.

months.summary: The best month. Skies are clear after the monsoon, harvests are under way and every trail is open. Manaslu and Larkya La are at their most reliable, Helambu's apples are ripe and Chisapani's sunrise views are sharp. Langtang depends on post-flood access to Syabrubesi; check current status before you travel.
months.tip: Book lodges on the Manaslu Circuit early for October.

months.weather: Kathmandu 8–22 °C; cold, clear nights up high
months.summary: Clear and cooler, with fewer crowds than October. Excellent for Langtang, Gosaikunda and Manaslu, though nights at Kyanjin and Bhimthang drop to minus 10 °C. Larkya La is usually crossable until early December. Nuwakot's ridge has clear Himalayan views at sunrise and oranges ripening on the slopes.
months.tip: Bring a warm sleeping bag and down jacket for high nights.

months.summary: Winter begins. Larkya La and Gosaikunda may close with snow, and many high lodges shut by late December. Lower routes shine: Chisapani, Helambu, Nuwakot and the Tamang Heritage Trail, with clear skies and quiet trails. Langtang is cold but possible to Kyanjin with good gear and current access.
months.tip: Choose routes below 3,700 m in winter unless you are well equipped.

faqs.q: Where are Langtang and Manaslu in Nepal?
faqs.a: They are the mountains directly north and north-west of Kathmandu. Langtang National Park, Gosaikunda and Helambu lie in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Sindhupalchok districts of Bagmati Province, 60 to 120 km from the capital. Manaslu and the Tsum Valley lie in Gorkha district of Gandaki Province, reached by road via Arughat.

faqs.q: Which is better, the Langtang or the Manaslu trek?
faqs.a: Langtang is shorter, 7 to 8 days, with no restricted permit and a maximum sleeping altitude of 3,870 m, ideal for a first Himalayan trek. Manaslu is a 14 to 16 day circuit crossing Larkya La at 5,106 m, needing restricted permits and more fitness. After August 2026, Langtang access is disrupted; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What happened in the August 2026 Rasuwa flood?
faqs.a: On 26 August 2026 a glacier collapse near Langtang Lirung sent a debris flood down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli, destroying the Rasuwagadhi border crossing, much of Syabrubesi, hydropower plants, roads and bridges into Nuwakot and beyond. More than 1,400 people were reported dead by late September and thousands missing. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is it safe to trek in Langtang now?
faqs.a: In September 2026 operators reported that the Langtang Valley trail above Syabrubesi was not directly damaged, but road access was cut and Syabrubesi badly damaged, and Nepal declared a disaster period. We only run Langtang trips when access and lodges are confirmed safe. Check current status before you travel; Helambu and Manaslu are alternatives.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide in Langtang and Manaslu?
faqs.a: Yes. Since April 2023 foreign trekkers in Nepal's national parks and conservation areas must trek with a licensed guide, which covers Langtang, Gosaikunda, Helambu and Shivapuri. Manaslu and Tsum are restricted areas that have always required a registered agency, a licensed guide and at least two trekkers. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Langtang and Manaslu?
faqs.a: October and November for clear skies and stable weather, and March to May for warm days and rhododendrons. December to February suits lower treks such as Helambu and Chisapani. June to September is monsoon, with rain, leeches and landslides, except for the Janai Purnima pilgrimage to Gosaikunda in August.

faqs.q: Are there short treks from Kathmandu in this region?
faqs.a: Yes. Chisapani is a one-night walk from Sundarijal on Kathmandu's edge. Helambu takes 5 to 8 days on foot from the city, with no flights and a high point of about 3,650 m. Nuwakot is a one or two night heritage trip by road. All three lie away from the 2026 flood zone, though roads to Nuwakot pass through it.

faqs.q: What permits are needed for the Manaslu Circuit?
faqs.a: The Manaslu restricted area permit, issued through a registered agency for at least two trekkers with a licensed guide; the Manaslu Conservation Area permit; and the Annapurna Conservation Area permit for the exit via Dharapani. Tsum Valley needs an additional restricted permit. Fees vary by season; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I combine Langtang, Gosaikunda and Helambu?
faqs.a: Yes. A classic 12 to 15 day trek walks up the Langtang Valley to Kyanjin Gompa, crosses to Gosaikunda via Thulo Syabru and Sing Gompa, goes over Lauribina La into Helambu and walks out to Sundarijal on the edge of Kathmandu. Road access at the Syabrubesi end depends on post-flood repairs; check current status before you travel.
